sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: In Mérignac the city handles street parking and the Métropole handles the rest. Street parking in the town centre is paid Monday to Saturday from 9:00 to 12:00 and 14:00 to 19:00 from 1 September to 31 July and free in August, with the first hour free once a day [0]. The post-parking charge is 30 euros, or 25 euros if paid within 24 hours [2]. Blue-disc zones with a 1h30 limit apply in Arlac, Chemin Long and Capeyron [3]. Because Bordeaux Métropole holds the mobility, parking and roads powers, the city council approved in 2021 a yearly agreement to pass its post-parking revenue to the Métropole, minus costs; the 2021 paper covered 2019 and the arrangement may have changed [4]. The Métropole's low-emission zone covers everything inside the ring road and, in its January 2026 version, bars only vehicles that cannot get a Crit'Air sticker; unclassified vehicles can still reach 11 park-and-rides, including Les Pins in Mérignac [6]. A mayoral order of April 2026 created a free five-minute carpool drop-off bay linked to the A10/A62 express carpool line [5].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The development is in the park-and-ride network and tram line F. On its own count Mérignac has five park-and-rides: Arlac (393 places), Quatre Chemins (393), Les Pins (220), Caroline Aigle (103) and the subscriber-only Mérignac Centre (276); TBM's own list gives 398 for Arlac and Quatre Chemins [7][8]. Same-day park-and-ride parking is included in a TBM subscription, and other users buy a ticket at 4.50 euros that gives seven round trips in a day for one to seven people [9]. Les Pins is one of six sites in a park-near-home offer for residents within 500 metres, at 300 euros a year [10]. Tram line F links the airport to central Bordeaux in about 35 minutes to Hôtel de Ville, according to the airport [16]. METPARK lists Mérignac Centre on its map of EV-equipped car parks, with 47 EV spaces according to the city [14][7].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
METPARK runs the 276-space underground Mérignac Centre car park, open 24/7, which doubles as a TBM park-and-ride for subscribers [11]. As the city shows its August 2026 rates, the first hour is free, then 2.40 euros for the first hour and 0.60 euro per 15 minutes, with a 9-euro 4-to-24-hour rate and free parking on Saturday mornings; subscriptions cost 70 euros a month, or 50 euros for residents [12]. A draft convention text published on the city site, unsigned in the copy read, provides for a three-year agreement from 1 May 2026 giving customers one free hour and compensating METPARK for it [13]. The airport runs its own car parks, with online-booking prices from 7 to 12 euros a day depending on the car park [15]. Klépierre reports 3,541 parking places at Mérignac Soleil [17].

Our data cover four car parks with 1,004 spaces from the Bordeaux Métropole feed, measured since 24 September 2026. Occupancy averaged about 18% on weekdays and 13% at weekends, weighted by spaces. Mérignac Centre (285 spaces in the feed) is the busiest at 34% and 35%, equal on weekdays and weekends. The park-and-rides are nearly empty: Quatre Chemins (396) averaged 18% on weekdays and 7% at weekends, Les Pins (220) 5% and Caroline Aigle (103) 4%. These are about four weeks of data.
